findings.evidence: alt="Product screenshot one" and alt="Product screenshot two"; both images fail to load (naturalWidth 0), so the alt text is all a sighted or screen-reader user gets, and it names a slot, not content.
findings.after: alt describing what the screen shows, e.g. alt="[DATA NEEDED: what the screenshot shows, e.g. the sync settings panel with two connected tools]"; fix the src so the file exists
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.1.1 Non-text Content: the alternative must serve the equivalent purpose.

findings.evidence: Inline svg with no aria-hidden, no role, no title or aria-label (dom-1440: name null, role null). It is decorative.
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.1.1 Non-text Content: decorative graphics must be hidden from assistive tech.

findings.evidence: Stylesheet: '.bar { animation: 2s ease 0s infinite normal none running grow; }'. The animation loops forever with no pause control; the sweep flagged the missing reduced-motion rule, this is the separate pause requirement. The bar renders with no visible height at capture, so impact may be nil; verify live.
findings.after: Remove the loop, or limit to animation-iteration-count: 1 and add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .bar { animation: none } }
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide: auto-moving content lasting over 5 seconds needs a way to stop it.

findings.evidence: A <button> outside any form with no stated destination; read out of context, 'Get started' does not say what starts (signup, demo, download). Only interactive element on the page.
findings.after: If it navigates, make it Start a free trial (or the real action); keep the visible text in the accessible name
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value: a navigating control should be a link whose name says where it goes.

findings.evidence: The h2 does not describe its section (features of what?), and the testimonial section has no heading. The eyebrow '01 / FEATURES' is a span, so the only descriptive word for the section is not in the heading tree.
findings.after:
Features

or an h2 naming what the features do; drop the eyebrow span
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.6 Headings and Labels: headings must describe topic or purpose.

strengths: The one control has a visible 2px solid ink focus outline (focus/00-on.png), and lang="en" and a title are set.
Main content is inside <main>; no content is hidden under reduced motion, observer-off or scripts-off (hidden.json all 241 chars).
